source: They’re typically on the cheaper end (around $20) and have the second highest percentage (21.4%) in the golden quadrant.

source: there are actually more songbirds with higher ratings than there are eagles, hawks, and other raptors

source: 65% of white wines with insects fell below the overall median rating of 4 stars. Red insect wines were a safer bet, with only 36% below 4 stars.

source: All the animals in this category were statistically more likely to be found on American, Australian, or Chilean wines than all wines, but by raw bottle counts the United States dominates.
claim: The United States accounts for 15 amphibian/reptile wines, more than any other country (Spain and Italy have 5 each).

source: France produced 33.6% percent of all animal wines in the dataset, but only 6.5% percent of cattle.
claim: 3 of 46 cattle wines (6.5%) are French.

source: Wines with sheep were statistically more likely to be priced between $10–19.99 (42% compared to 25% of all wines)
claim: 24 of 57 sheep wines (42.1%) are priced between $10 and $19.99.

source: Italy had a statistically higher percentage of mythical wines than all wines (30% compared to 21%).
claim: 37 of 123 mythical-creature wines (30.1%) are Italian.

source: The majority of these wines are from the Mediterranean region (France, Italy, and Spain) or from New Zealand.
claim: 27 of 33 marine-invertebrate wines (81.8%) are from France, Italy, Spain or New Zealand.

source: The wines follow a logarithmic trend, where rating increases with price, but with diminishing returns.
claim: A least-squares fit of rating on log(price) for animal wines priced at or below $150 has a positive slope of 0.293, so rating rises with price at a diminishing rate.

source: Across all categories and variables, the only dataset that maintained its price as the quality increased was New Zealand wines.
claim: New Zealand is the only country whose animal wines have a negative least-squares price-on-rating slope (-7.42 dollars per star); every other country has a positive slope.
